findings.title: Make the other binding Git rules agree with member commits
findings.evidence: §5 rule 2 now reserves committing for the captain 'in the main checkout (single git writer per worktree; a member commits only in its own worktree)'; §5 rule 5 now says members 'may commit inside their own worktree; the captain alone commits in the main checkout and merges'. Consistent with the §5 ONE-git-writer bullet (AGENTS.md:282-286).

findings.title: Guard the mpdConfig lookup so an absent service cannot abort apply
findings.evidence: effectiveConfig wraps ctx.get("mpdConfig") in try/catch, requires typeof service.get === "function", and catches every worktree.* leaf read, so apply keeps the row config instead of aborting before the five tools register.
findings.test: worktree.test.ts 'effectiveConfig falls back to the row config when the mpdConfig lookup throws'

findings.title: Bound Git execution time
findings.evidence: runGit spawns with timeout: GIT_TIMEOUT_MS (30_000) and killSignal SIGKILL, maps ETIMEDOUT to the distinct GIT_TIMEOUT_CODE (-2, documented as distinct from -1 spawn failure) and writes 'git timed out after <n>ms' to stderr.
findings.test: worktree.test.ts 'a stalled git is killed at the bound and reports a DISTINCT timeout code' (fake sleep-5 git, 100 ms bound, asserts -2 and not -1)

findings.title: Recover the worktree if recording its creation fails
findings.evidence: createEntry wraps writeIndex; on failure it removes the just-added worktree (removeWorktreePath force) and deletes the branch it created (deleteBranch force; skipped on a reattach so existing commits survive), logging a rollback failure instead of swallowing it.
findings.test: worktree.test.ts 'removes the just-added worktree and branch when recording it fails' (both gone; the same create succeeds after the obstruction is removed)

findings.title: Revalidate the stored target before removal
findings.evidence: removeWorktree re-canonicalises the repo and asserts workspace containment, requires isUnderRoot(worktreeDir(deps), entry.path), and refuses when git worktree list does not report the recorded path (unregistered-worktree). The stored branch remains trusted — pre-existing, raised as N1.
findings.test: worktree.test.ts 'refuses a recorded path outside the worktree root' and 'refuses an existing recorded path git does not list as a worktree'

findings.title: Keep a failed branch deletion retryable
findings.evidence: WorktreeEntry/RemoveResult gained branchPending; the terminal early-return skips only status removed WITH the flag clear, so a second remove retries the branch and clears the flag on success.
findings.test: worktree.test.ts 'keeps a failed branch deletion retryable instead of a terminal tombstone' (ref lock; branchDeleted=false + branchPending=true, then the retry deletes the branch and clears the flag)

findings.title: Confirm Git still manages a reused member directory
findings.evidence: isGitManaged (canonical recorded path vs git worktree list --porcelain) guards both member lookups (createForMember returns an existing checkout only when managed; cwdForMember returns a path only when managed) and recordOf's dirty.
findings.test: worktree.test.ts 'member lookups ignore a directory git no longer registers as a worktree' and 'refuses an existing recorded path git does not list as a worktree'

findings.title: Reattach the branch when a member directory has vanished
findings.evidence: createForMember keeps the stale record, prunes only when the recorded repo still resolves and is contained, and re-creates with reattachBranch (attachWorktree, no -b) + replaceKey; git refuses an unsafe attach and the record is replaced only on success.
findings.test: worktree.test.ts 're-attaches the existing branch when a member directory vanished, preserving its commits' (HEAD and file survive) and 'does not reattach a branch another worktree already has checked out' (degrades, then succeeds once freed)

findings.title: Refresh read-only classification after an unavailable roster read (additional comment in the review body)
findings.evidence: rosterReadonlyKeys answers undefined when mpdRoles is absent or list() throws; memberWorktreeLookup retries the read on every member until one succeeds and only then caches readonlyKeys.

newIssues.what: The stored record's branch is still trusted: readIndex validates field types only, and removeWorktree deletes entry.branch with git branch -d|-D while mergeWorktree merges it. A tampered <ws>/.mpd/worktrees/index.json (writable by a member, whose sandbox is the parent workspace per D1) can make the captain's forced removal delete an unrelated local branch, or make a merge bring in an arbitrary branch. git protects only the branch checked out in the main worktree.
newIssues.direction: Revalidate entry.branch before use: isValidBranch, the branch git -C <path> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD actually reports for that worktree, and a refusal for protectedBranches / the main checkout's HEAD.
newIssues.whyNotFail: Present at HEAD before the fix wave; CR [14] named the path, not the branch.

newIssues.what: existed = typeof worktree.cwdForMember === 'function' && cwdForMember(...) !== undefined. A partial service view without cwdForMember yields created=true, so a failed spawn would release a possibly REUSED checkout; the adjacent throw path already fails safe (existed = true).
newIssues.direction: Default existed to true when the probe is not a function.

newIssues.what: Both fakes build paths from the RAW member name ('Senior Engineer') and their comments claim they are 'derived key/path exactly as Lane A builds it', but Lane A slugifies ('senior-engineer', proven by worktree.test.ts). The arms remain valid for request passthrough; the stated fact is wrong.
newIssues.direction: Either slugify in the fakes or soften the comment to 'the path the service returned'.

newIssues.what: No test exercises the production call site: the only reseed arm passes worktreeTeamId directly to promoteAfterHandoff, so a revert to caller.cell.teamId would keep the suite green.
newIssues.direction: Drive the barrier once with a legacy cell + an execution team and assert the lookup is addressed with the resolved id.

newIssues.what: The official-executor arm of the add_member spawn site is untested; only the approval site's official arm is covered.
newIssues.direction: Add the append arm with an official-kind executor and assert no worktree call, no cwd, one line.

newIssues.what: Recorded paths are handed out after existsSync + isGitManaged without re-asserting isUnderRoot; D2 is enforced at CREATE only, so a tampered index can redirect a member's cwd.
newIssues.direction: Re-assert the workspace containment on lookup as well.

newIssues.what: A leftover directory at the member path that git does not manage permanently blocks recovery for that pair (path-exists every attempt, degrade each spawn). Fail-closed and logged, but not documented.
newIssues.direction: Name it in the docs bounds, or offer an explicit operator remedy.

newIssues.what: Each worktree.* leaf is read twice (typeof check then value), so a mutating getter could merge an inconsistent value.
newIssues.direction: Read each leaf once into a local.

declined: Repo-containment refusing member worktrees when the workspace is a strict subdirectory of a git repo — CR-directed, safe-degrading (D4) and documented in all four docs; not a defect of this wave.

const backend = deps.executor() hoisted to once per approval — the adapter's teamExecutor() is total and stable per composition; no observable regression, and the worktree decision must use the same backend as the spawn.
Cleanup through a nested dsh.executeTool('mpd_worktree_remove') instead of a service method — a legitimate use of Lane A's own tool; refusal is logged, never fatal.
An empty-but-successful roster read is cached as an empty set (no member classified read-only) — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty roster here; fail-open is the documented rule.
worktree.max 0.5 defaulting to 32 rather than being rejected — the CR body's own remedy was 'default values whose floored result is less than one'; a boot refusal would be worse.
152 pre-existing extensionless relative specifiers in the three touched packages — AGENTS.md §6's packages/*/src clause permits them; only the 5 CR-flagged NEW specifiers were changed (minimal diff).

A writeTeam/updateTeamMember throw AFTER a successful spawn would now also release the created worktree — the member row is already dropped on that path (pre-existing) so the child is orphaned either way; unreachable in practice (pure store writes).
The repo tool-parameter description does not restate the containment rule — the refusal sentence names it and the docs carry it.
Mixed .ts / extensionless specifiers in team-core's index.ts — no gate covers specifier form; cosmetic only.
